title: Pasta Puttanesca
subtitle: Neapolitan pasta with olives, capers, and anchovies
excerpt: The assertively flavoured pasta of Naples: spaghetti sauced with tinned tomatoes, black olives, capers, anchovies, and chilli, all of which come from the store cupboard. Ready in under 20 minutes with a flavour punch out of all proportion to its speed.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pasta puttanesca (the name is typically translated as 'whore's pasta', though the etymology is disputed) is a twentieth-century Neapolitan dish, first documented in writing in the 1960s. The story that it was invented by a brothel owner who needed to cook quickly between clients is probably apocryphal; more likely it is simply a quick supper dish made entirely from store-cupboard ingredients that could be assembled at any time without a trip to market. The combination of anchovies, capers, olives, tomatoes, garlic, and chilli produces an intensely savoury, pungent sauce that requires no parmesan. The dish can be made with any pasta but is most traditionally served with spaghetti.

content.text: Taste before seasoning: anchovies, capers, and olives are all very salty. The sauce may need no additional salt at all. Cook the sauce quickly over high heat; it should not stew. Add the pasta straight from the cooking water without rinsing so the starch helps bind the sauce.

Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the garlic, anchovies, and chilli flakes. Cook for 1 minute, stirring, until the anchovies dissolve into the oil. Add the tinned tomatoes and cook over medium-high heat for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly reduced.
Add the olives and capers. Cook for 3 more minutes. Taste and add salt only if needed; the anchovies, olives, and capers provide considerable salt.

Cook the pasta in well-salted water until al dente. Reserve 80 ml of cooking water. Drain and add to the sauce. Toss over high heat for 1 minute, adding pasta water to loosen. Scatter with parsley and serve immediately. No cheese.
